memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They are to be responsible to you and are to perform all the duties of the tent, but they must not go near the furnishings of the sanctuary or the altar. Otherwise both they and you will die. They are to join you and be responsible for the care of the tent of meeting — all the work at the tent — and no one else may come near where you are. You are to perform the duties of the sanctuary and the altar, so that my wrath will not fall on the Israelites again. I myself have selected your fellow Levites from among the Israelites as a gift to you, dedicated to the Lord to do the work at the tent of meeting." — Num 18:3-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God carefully assigns boundaries. The Levites would serve, but they must not approach the most holy furnishings; that was reserved for the priests alone. These were not arbitrary restrictions but loving safeguards, given "so that my wrath will not fall on the Israelites again." God was protecting His people by teaching them to honour what is holy.

We sometimes chafe at boundaries, imagining that limits are unkind. But here we see that God's boundaries are acts of love. He knew that treating holy things carelessly would bring harm, so He drew clear lines to keep His people safe. The limits were not to shut people out coldly, but to preserve them from destruction.

There is wisdom here for how we live. God's commands and boundaries are never meant to rob us of joy but to guard our lives. Like a loving parent who fences a yard beside a busy road, God sets limits because He knows what will harm us. To honour His boundaries is to trust His heart.

Notice too that God calls the Levites "a gift" — first a gift to Aaron, and dedicated to the Lord. Even the labour of serving God was framed as a gift, not a burden. And in Christ, all of this finds its fulfilment. He perfectly honoured the Father's holiness, and through Him the barriers that once kept people at a distance have been dealt with. The curtain has been opened, not by ignoring God's holiness, but because Christ satisfied it. What the Levites guarded from afar, we now approach through Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you view God's boundaries as restrictions or as loving protection?
2. Where might honouring God's limits actually be guarding your life?
3. How does Christ open the way to God while still honouring His holiness?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your boundaries flow from love and are meant to protect me. Help me to trust Your heart and honour Your ways. Thank You that in Christ the way to You is opened, Your holiness fully satisfied. Amen.
